integrity_statement: This append-only checkpoint records fourteen structured rhetorical analyses after passage-by-passage review of two complete long-form texts already admitted in the journal-gated foundation. It stores analytical moves, ordering rules, and prohibitions rather than copied prose or runtime facts. The two texts are not additional admissions and do not change the thirty-source or 120-observation counts.

long_form_rhetorical_analysis.requirement: Approximately fourteen passage analyses across two complete long-form texts, balanced from person-level adoption measurement through task-level productivity and macroeconomic aggregation

source_selection.title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI
source_selection.publisher: Management Science / Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
source_selection.substantive_extent: Complete 53-page October 2025 author manuscript reconciled to the published Management Science record
source_selection.selection_basis: A nationally representative adoption study that demonstrates how to move from survey design and mutually distinct use states through frequency, intensity, task mix, workplace policy, self-reported time savings, and explicitly modeled productivity potential.

source_selection.title: The Simple Macroeconomics of AI
source_selection.publisher: Economic Policy / National Bureau of Economic Research
source_selection.substantive_extent: Complete 46-page published article and 49-page author manuscript, including task model, calibration, wage analysis, appendices, and journal discussions
source_selection.selection_basis: A task-based macroeconomic analysis that demonstrates how to aggregate bounded micro evidence while preserving adoption, feasibility, task difficulty, capital response, wage incidence, GDP, and welfare as separate reasoning stages.

passages.rhetorical_job: Establishes the survey frame and external benchmarks before presenting an adoption rate.
passages.claim_move: Defines a repeated national survey of U.S. adults ages 18-64 and explains how the focal waves were pooled.
passages.evidence_move: Reports recruitment, wave sizes, CPS-aligned questions, raking weights, response-quality screens, and validation against employment, earnings, occupation, and industry distributions.
passages.qualification_move: States that the commercial online panel is not a random population sample and identifies the weighting and validation steps used to bound that limitation.
passages.production_use: Introduce adoption evidence with population, dates, survey mode, sample construction, and validation benchmark before the headline share.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not call a weighted online survey a census or omit its target population and field dates.

passages.rhetorical_job: Defines awareness, work use, nonwork use, frequency, and intensity as separate observable states.
passages.claim_move: Adapts historical CPS technology-use questions while supplying respondents with a concrete definition and examples of generative AI.
passages.evidence_move: Uses sequenced questions that preserve employed-worker and all-adult denominators and reserve intensity and time-savings questions for reported users.
passages.qualification_move: Treats passive or embedded AI that respondents may not recognize as missing from the measure, making observed adoption a lower bound on aware use.
passages.production_use: Name the exact use state and denominator every time an adoption rate appears.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not collapse awareness, any use, work use, weekly use, daily use, and embedded exposure into one adoption number.

passages.rhetorical_job: Makes a historical comparison legible without equating unlike technologies or their benefits.
passages.claim_move: Aligns adoption observations by years since a first mass-market release and separates overall, work, and nonwork use.
passages.evidence_move: Uses nearly parallel survey wording for generative AI and personal computers and discloses the selected launch dates and comparison years.
passages.qualification_move: Explains that lower price, mobility, and ease of use can accelerate uptake, so a similar work-adoption share does not imply equivalent productive value.
passages.production_use: When comparing diffusion curves, state the launch convention, elapsed time, question wording, use context, and cost regime.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not convert faster user uptake than an older technology into a forecast of equal or greater productivity.

passages.rhetorical_job: Moves from a national average to the worker and task composition beneath it.
passages.claim_move: Separates demographic, earnings, occupation, predicted exposure, reported usefulness, and actual adoption patterns.
passages.evidence_move: Reports distinct subgroup rates and compares occupation-level realized adoption with two task-exposure indices and workers' own usefulness assessments.
passages.qualification_move: Calls exposure informative but incomplete where occupations with similar predicted exposure have sharply different realized use.
passages.production_use: Use exposure as one explanatory layer and require observed use, task context, and worker distribution before making a diffusion claim.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not narrate an exposure score as adoption or hide distributional gaps behind the national mean.

passages.rhetorical_job: Introduces the organizational gate between an individually accessible tool and productive workplace use.
passages.claim_move: Distinguishes perceived lack of usefulness from employer bans, ambiguous rules, coworker pressure, privacy concerns, and missing know-how.
passages.evidence_move: Relates reported barriers and employer encouragement to occupation-level and individual use, then adds demographic, occupation, and exposure controls.
passages.qualification_move: Explicitly warns that employer encouragement is highly predictive but not necessarily causal because job roles and management context may be jointly selected.
passages.production_use: Name the organizational mechanism and evidence tier when connecting firm policy to worker adoption.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not convert a large conditional association with employer encouragement into a causal managerial effect.

passages.section: Frequency, intensity, and reported time savings
passages.rhetorical_job: Builds an intensity ladder before translating use into a productivity-related quantity.
passages.claim_move: Separates days used, minutes actively using the tool, share of work hours assisted, and counterfactual hours reportedly saved.
passages.evidence_move: Constructs lower and upper bounds from categorical time intervals and calculates user-only and all-worker denominators separately.
passages.qualification_move: Labels time savings self-reported, caps open-ended responses conservatively, and does not treat assisted hours as automated hours.
passages.production_use: Move from adoption to frequency to intensity to reported time saved; retain the user and workforce denominators at each step.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not multiply any-use prevalence by a laboratory productivity estimate while skipping observed intensity.

passages.rhetorical_job: Marks the boundary where descriptive survey evidence enters an economic model.
passages.claim_move: Translates wage-weighted reported time savings into effective labor and potential output under a stated production function.
passages.evidence_move: Shows each bridge term—use, time saved, wages, labor share, and sector aggregation—and compares the implied micro magnitude with separate aggregate data and prior experiments.
passages.qualification_move: Calls the result potential, holds total factor productivity, capital, and hours fixed, and excludes delayed gains from firm-wide automation and reorganization.
passages.production_use: Signal the switch from observed input to modeled implication and list the assumptions carrying the translation.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not publish a model-implied productivity gain as an observed contribution to current national productivity.

passages.rhetorical_job: Converts a diffuse argument about transformative AI into a bounded question that can be decomposed.
passages.claim_move: Separates technological capability from the macroeconomic size and timing of productivity, wage, and inequality effects.
passages.evidence_move: Contrasts prominent external forecasts with a task-based accounting structure and identifies the empirical inputs each projection requires.
passages.qualification_move: Keeps singularity-scale possibilities outside the calibrated exercise and labels medium-run estimates as scenarios with uncertain inputs.
passages.production_use: Replace broad transformation language with the affected object, transmission mechanism, horizon, and evidence class.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not answer capability spectacle with an unbounded GDP claim.

passages.rhetorical_job: Defines the unit of analysis and keeps automation, task complementarity, new tasks, and factor responses distinct.
passages.claim_move: Represents output through tasks that can be assigned to labor, capital, or AI and traces the effect of lowering a task's cost.
passages.evidence_move: Derives separate comparative-static channels for cost savings, factor demand, wages, capital adjustment, and the creation of new good or bad tasks.
passages.qualification_move: Conditions the clean aggregation on competitive equilibrium and on micro effects operating through measurable task-level cost reductions.
passages.production_use: Identify whether evidence concerns automation of an existing task, complementarity, capital deepening, or creation of a new task before aggregating it.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not use one task-level productivity estimate to represent every macroeconomic channel.

passages.rhetorical_job: Shows precisely how local cost savings receive economy-wide weights.
passages.claim_move: Aggregates task-level productivity through the fraction of affected activity and the initial expenditure or factor shares attached to it.
passages.evidence_move: Expresses the first-order TFP effect as an economically weighted sum rather than a simple average of experiment results.
passages.qualification_move: Makes the result local to the baseline allocation and separates the direct TFP term from later investment and reallocation responses.
passages.production_use: Require an affected share, a task-level effect, an economic weight, and a horizon before moving from micro evidence to macro magnitude.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not apply a micro percentage to all work, all labor, or GDP without the correct exposure and value-share denominator.

passages.rhetorical_job: Prevents the best-measured task class from silently standing in for the unmeasured remainder.
passages.claim_move: Distinguishes tasks with clear outcomes and learnable mappings from context-dependent tasks with ambiguous success measures.
passages.evidence_move: Reviews the task structure of early experiments, then classifies exposed task statements through verbs, work activities, topic clusters, and a manually trained assignment process.
passages.qualification_move: Discloses judgment calls, ambiguous classifications, and assumed rather than observed productivity for hard tasks.
passages.production_use: Attach every productivity result to its task frontier and state whether the target tasks share its feedback and measurability conditions.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not generalize evidence from writing, coding, or scripted support tasks to diagnosis, care, hiring, advising, or other open-ended work without a frontier test.

passages.rhetorical_job: Turns a numerical scenario into a transparent product of assumptions and then attacks its upper bound.
passages.claim_move: Combines feasible task exposure, economic weights, and assumed cost savings over a ten-year horizon.
passages.evidence_move: Uses separate exposure studies and micro experiments, then tests alternative feasibility and cost-decline assumptions.
passages.qualification_move: Identifies sparse firm investment, possible provider concentration, organizational adjustment costs, J-curve timing, and hard-task uncertainty as downward risks not fully captured in the calculation.
passages.production_use: Present macro estimates as a parameter stack and state which adoption and organizational frictions remain outside it.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not call an exposure-and-cost calibration an observed forecast path or use the J-curve to guarantee later payoff.

passages.section: TFP, GDP, wages, inequality, and welfare
passages.rhetorical_job: Keeps multiple economic outcomes and their incidence from collapsing into one gain number.
passages.claim_move: Moves separately from direct TFP to capital response and GDP, from task displacement to group wages, and from measured output to welfare when new tasks create harms.
passages.evidence_move: Uses model-specific factor shares, demographic exposure patterns, substitution parameters, and illustrative bad-task calculations for different outcome layers.
passages.qualification_move: Labels distributional and welfare calculations more uncertain than the direct cost-savings channel and treats negative-social-value estimates as illustrative.
passages.production_use: State who receives the gain and whether the quantity is TFP, GDP, labor income, capital income, consumer value, or welfare.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not infer worker benefit, lower inequality, or higher welfare from higher output alone.

passages.rhetorical_job: Closes by reconciling technological promise with the evidentiary limits of the calibrated result.
passages.claim_move: Organizes potential macro effects into productivity, wages and inequality, and harmful new tasks, then states which channels were modeled.
passages.evidence_move: Returns to the task share, cost-saving evidence, task difficulty, investment response, and distributional inputs developed earlier.
passages.qualification_move: Preserves revolutionary outcomes as logically possible but currently unevidenced, and avoids treating medium-run estimates as a ceiling on all future innovation.
passages.production_use: End an Economic Impact Read with the strongest supported transmission claim, the binding uncertainty, and the outcome not yet observed.
passages.anti_pattern: Do not end with either inevitability or dismissal when the evidence supports a bounded, conditional result.

cross_text_production_rules: Define the population, observation window, use state, and denominator before reporting adoption.
Move through awareness, access, actual use, frequency, intensity, task breadth, reported time savings, workflow integration, and realized outcome without skipping states.
Keep worker adoption, employer deployment, and organization-wide redesign distinct.
Treat task exposure as a prior for where use may occur, never as observed use or realized productivity.
Separate assisted hours, time saved, effective labor, measured labor productivity, TFP, GDP, wages, profit, and welfare.
Mark the exact point at which observed evidence enters a model and list the exposure, economic-weight, substitution, capital, and horizon assumptions.
Qualify every task result by capability frontier, outcome observability, context dependence, and error cost.
Trace incidence across workers, firms, capital owners, consumers, and society instead of assigning all value to one beneficiary.
Use cross-sectional associations and self-reports as bounded evidence, not causal proof.
Close with the demonstrated bottleneck and the next realization evidence required; never fill an unobserved link with inevitability.
